name: Brown Yellow
lede: Brown Yellow names a yellow pulled toward brown, recorded by the xkcd 2010 crowd color survey and otherwise undocumented in the books behind this archive.

sections.title: A crowd name with old neighbors
sections.body: No dictionary or paint-brand plate carries this exact compound; it is modifier grammar, first written down in the 2010 xkcd survey [1]. Its nearest named neighbors are startlingly close: [[ocher|Ocher]], 3.1 units away, and [[pyrite-yellow|Pyrite Yellow]], 5.0 units away, both read as close to this exact color [2]. [[dark-mustard|Dark Mustard]] and plain [[mustard]] sit further out, both darker or lighter by comparison [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
This color appears in 70 of our 23,781 paintings, about 0.29 percent, more common than 54 percent of our named colors, as photographed [3]. It peaks in paintings from the 1900s, 1.7 times the rate expected from that century's share of the archive, and it is most over-represented in Indian paintings, at 4.4 times the expected rate [3]. Luis Egidio Meléndez is its most devoted painter here, with 4 of his 39 works carrying it, 6.5 times his baseline [3].

The earliest match is a 1403 panel by Gherardo Starnina, 607 years before the xkcd survey; our archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first [3]. In printed English the bare phrase "brown yellow" peaked around 1800, across all its senses, which can include uses that have nothing to do with naming a color [3].
